title: Mag-Mamba: Modeling Coupled Spatio-temporal Asymmetry for POI Recommendation

problem.claim: POI recommendation must address coupled spatiotemporal asymmetry in urban mobility, including location-transition intents that are asymmetric and conditioned on time.

gap.claim: Existing graph- and sequence-based methods struggle to unify time-varying global directionality because they rely on symmetric operators or real-valued aggregations.

contributions.claim: Mag-Mamba models spatiotemporal asymmetry as phase-driven rotational dynamics in the complex domain.

A Time-conditioned Magnetic Phase Encoder constructs a time-conditioned Magnetic Laplacian on the geographic adjacency graph using edge phase differences to characterize evolving spatial directionality.
A Complex-valued Mamba module extends scalar state decay to joint decay-rotation dynamics modulated by time intervals and magnetic geographic priors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets.
The authors report significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: POI recommendation faces coupled spatiotemporal asymmetry in urban mobility.
Existing graph and sequence backbones struggle to model time-varying global directionality.
Mag-Mamba represents spatiotemporal asymmetry as complex-domain phase-driven rotational dynamics.
The framework combines a time-conditioned magnetic phase encoder with a complex-valued Mamba module.
Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported to improve performance over state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: The framework represents directional, time-varying mobility patterns with phase-based complex dynamics.

interpretation.claim: When transitions are directional and temporally conditioned, asymmetric operators may capture structure that symmetric aggregation obscures.

application.claim: Consider time-conditioned directional or phase-based representations for recommendation problems involving evolving transition intent.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond POI recommendation or other mobility settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, sizes, evaluation metrics, or numerical improvements.
